sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a gentle, round, blue plesiosaur with a cream belly and darker blue spots, swimming, turned a little to the left, its long neck curving up to a small round head. Draw this exact plesiosaur as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the plump oval body with its cream belly and its darker blue spots, turned as in image 1, without head, without neck, without flippers and without tail: no flippers drawn on it, the cream belly one smooth round shape. At the front top, only the very base of the neck rises out of the body, a short stump about half as tall as the neck is wide, cream in front and spotted blue behind, as wide as the neck is where it meets the body in image 1; the stump ends in a soft edge cut straight across with NO outline (the neck tucks under it). At the back, the spotted back runs on smoothly into the very root of the tail and ends there in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no round bump, no stump, no line where the tail would join. The drawing's dark outline runs only along the front of the chest, round the belly and along the back.
2. the neck alone: the long, smooth, curving neck of image 1, cream in front and spotted blue behind, curving exactly as in image 1, drawn whole from its base (normally hidden inside the body) up to just under the head, without the head; both of its ends a soft edge cut straight across with NO outline, the dark outline running only down its two sides.
3. the head alone, without neck: the small round head with its rounded snout, its two little nostrils, its spots and its rosy cheek, turned as in image 1, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth and no mouth line, the snout and the cream chin one smooth shape. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head, round the snout and along the chin, as in image 1. From the chin round to the back of the head its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the cream throat and the blue back of the head simply stop there, a little below the rosy cheek.
4. the far front flipper: the big soft paddle flipper on the left of image 1, reaching out to the left from behind the chest, drawn whole from its rounded root (normally hidden behind the chest) to its rounded tip, blue with spots on top and cream along its underside, as in image 1; its root a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
5. the near front flipper: the big soft paddle flipper in the middle of image 1, in front of the belly, reaching down and back, drawn whole from its rounded shoulder to its rounded tip, blue with spots and cream along its edge, its rounded shoulder with its outline as in image 1.
6. the near hind flipper: the big soft paddle flipper on the right of image 1, reaching back, drawn whole from its rounded root (normally hidden in the body) to its rounded tip, blue with spots and cream along its underside, as in image 1; its root a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
7. the far hind flipper: the same big soft paddle flipper of the other side, a little smaller as it is farther away, reaching down and back, drawn whole from its rounded root to its rounded tip; its root a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
8. the tail: the short spotted tail with its cream underside, curving up to its rounded tip as in image 1, drawn whole from its thick base (normally hidden inside the body) to the tip; its base a soft edge cut straight across with NO outline.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no claws. No water, no text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a gentle, round, blue plesiosaur; image 2 shows the same plesiosaur cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the plesiosaur's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the plesiosaur in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, near the snout) is smaller than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look to the left and a little up: each dark iris sits towards the left of its eye, the white on its right.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a dark-brown round iris with a white sparkle, looking to the left and a little up.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U.
4. sad: open and round, a soft warm-brown iris with a white sparkle and a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim, looking a little down and to the left; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, to the left, the iris towards the left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, mouths, without the nostrils, none with any teeth: 17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a thin, closed, gently smiling line curling up at its right end. 18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, the inside pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth. 19. the mouth puckered into a small round 'o', the inside pink, as for blowing bubbles. 20. the mouth in a small sad frown. 21. the mouth wide open in a big round 'O', as for a big yawn, the inside pink with a little tongue, no teeth. 22. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a gentle, round, blue plesiosaur; image 2 shows the same plesiosaur cut into puppet parts. Draw one single piece, centred on the sheet: the plesiosaur's head alone, exactly the head at the top left of image 2 — the same small round blue head, the same rounded snout with its two little nostrils, the same darker blue spots and rosy cheek, turned the same way, the same drawing style, colours, texture and line, at the size it has in image 2 — but with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, and NO mouth: no smile line, no line at all across the snout or the cheek; the blue snout and the cream chin below it meet softly, the blue simply fading into the cream with no line between them. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head, round the snout and along the bottom of the chin, as in image 2. From the chin round to the back of the head its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline, as in image 2. Nothing else on the sheet. No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the plesiosaur swims along to the left, its long neck held high and its four big flippers stroking slowly under the water, then stops.
the plesiosaur nods yes, twice, dipping its little head on its long neck.
the plesiosaur shakes its little head no.
the plesiosaur turns its long neck to look one way, then the other, then back.
the plesiosaur laughs and laughs, bobbing in the water with giggles.
the plesiosaur talks, its mouth moving, its little head bobbing.
the plesiosaur cries, its head hanging low, bobbing in the water with little sobs.

pause.shows: the plesiosaur crying, its head hanging low, eyes squeezed shut with tears

animations.description: the plesiosaur gives a big yawn, lets its long neck droop and dozes on the water, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: the plesiosaur fast asleep on the water, eyes shut, its neck drooped

animations.description: the plesiosaur sways gently from side to side in the water, its long neck swaying like a dancer.
the plesiosaur lifts a big front flipper out of the water and waves hello.
the plesiosaur dips its head and dives under the water with a few bubbles, then pops up again with a happy grin.
the plesiosaur lifts a front flipper and slaps the water, splash, then does it again and laughs.
the plesiosaur rises up tall out of the water, stretching its long neck high to look far away, then settles back down.

pause.shows: the plesiosaur risen up tall, its long neck stretched high, looking far away

animations.description: the plesiosaur puckers its mouth into a little o and blows bubbles, puff, puff, puff, then smiles.

pause.shows: the plesiosaur with its mouth a round little o, blowing bubbles

animations.description: the plesiosaur floats still on the water with its eyes closed, face up to the sun, calm and relaxed, then opens its eyes happily.

pause.shows: the plesiosaur floating still on the water, eyes closed, face up, relaxed
